responsibilities: Conduct deep, hypothesis-driven exploratory data analysis to support discovery, research, and operational decision-making.
Translate ambiguous business questions into structured analysis.
Serve as a partner to discovery team, providing analytics support.
Design, develop, and deliver high-quality dashboards, reports, and ad-hoc analyses with fast turnaround times.
Produce executive- and stakeholder ready outputs with minimal rework.
Balance speed and rigor while maintaining high standards of data quality.
Develop complex SQL queries and conduct performance and quality checks.
Use Python for data analysis, feature engineering, and analytical modeling.
Build reusable analytical assets to accelerate future discovery efforts.
Collaborate and support data science team in developing AI/ML uses cases.
Apply statistical experimentation modeling techniques where appropriate.
Maintain active curiosity and learning in analytics, data science, and AI.
Partner closely with business stakeholders, discovery team to align analytics solutions with business objectives.
Clearly communicate analytical findings, assumptions, and limitations to technical and non-technical audiences.
Contribute to Agile/SCRUM ceremonies and deliver work predictably within sprint commitments.
Continuously improve analytics processes, tooling, and delivery practices.
Support modernization and migration initiatives from legacy reporting platforms.
Participate in on-call or escalation support rotations as needed.
Mentor peers on analytics best practices when appropriate.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Balance speed and rigor while maintaining high standards of data quality.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The posting names the trade-off outright — a whole section called "Rapid Analytics Delivery" with "fast turnaround times" sits against quality checks, validation and governance.
evidence.domain_risk: delivering 500,000 lifesaving blood products annually to 150+ hospitals, EMS and healthcare partners
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: A healthcare organisation, but the role's own language is discovery and research analytics with no compliance, audit or regulatory requirement stated.
evidence.collaboration_width: discovery team; research teams; data science team
evidence.data_team_maturity: Support modernization and migration initiatives from legacy reporting platforms.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A separate data science team, sprint ceremonies and on-call rotations exist, but a legacy reporting estate is still being migrated.
evidence.jd_authorship: Use Python for data analysis, feature engineering, and analytical modeling.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Feature engineering and statistical experimentation are concrete, but most bullets are generic delivery language under HR-style section headers.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Serve as a partner to discovery team, providing analytics support.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Weight splits between the discovery and research teams the analyses serve and the data science team whose AI/ML use cases this role supports.
evidence.autonomy_level: The Analytics Engineer operates with a high degree of independence, demonstrates strong ownership of outcomes
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: High independence and problem-definition ownership sit against sprint commitments, on-call rotations and translating questions handed over by stakeholders.
evidence.ai_role: Collaborate and support data science team in developing AI/ML uses cases.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds the analytical assets and feature work that the data science team's AI/ML use cases run on.
evidence.testing_framing: Develop complex SQL queries and conduct performance and quality checks.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Running quality checks is written in as the candidate's own action, backed by a data validation and governance requirement.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Participate in on-call or escalation support rotations as needed.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: On-call rotations and rework avoidance signal operational reliability concern, secondary to a delivery-first framing.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Support modernization and migration initiatives from legacy reporting platforms.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Building reusable analytical assets sits alongside migrating away from legacy reporting platforms.
evidence.work_arrangement: Work Location: Hybrid, Remote, or On-Site.
evidence.loss_aversion: "Produce executive- and stakeholder ready outputs with minimal rework" — rework in front of executives is the named failure to avoid.
